agent_requirement.reason: Agents generating or modifying TypeScript must run Biome lint + tsc before declaring work complete — type errors and lint violations caught at write time, not review time
agent_requirement.how: biome check --write <file> && tsc --noEmit — fix all errors; suppress only with // biome-ignore <rule>: <rationale>

claude_code.mechanism: LSP servers are Claude Code plugins from the `claude-plugins-official` marketplace, enabled per-user via `enabledPlugins` in ~/.claude/settings.json (e.g. `"typescript-lsp@claude-plugins-official": true`). This is a per-machine setting — it does NOT propagate to other developers or to cloud-hosted/headless agents automatically. Each human (or machine) using Claude Code interactively needs to enable it once.
claude_code.scope_reason: Owner ruling 2026-07-25: TypeScript and Python are in broad enough use across this org's repos to justify a user-level default (every session on this machine gets them, no per-repo action needed). Go and Rust are NOT in broad enough use yet to justify the same — see go.yaml/rust.yaml's own scope_reason, which enable those two per-project instead. Revisit this split if usage patterns shift.
claude_code.future_direction: Manually toggling enabledPlugins in ~/.claude/settings.json is a stopgap. The intended end state is an org-side mechanism (an intelligence-packet style injection, or a future dedicated MCP server) detecting a project's language(s) and ensuring the right LSP plugin is active automatically, instead of a human maintaining this by hand -- platform-side work, not a local settings concern. Not built as of 2026-07-25; tracked as a real ask, not assumed done.
claude_code.no_biome_lsp: There is no dedicated Biome LSP plugin in this marketplace as of 2026-07-25. Biome stays enforced via CI (`biome ci`) and the pre-push hook (agent_requirement above), not via live diagnostics.
claude_code.typescript_gotcha: typescript-lsp initializes a real tsserver, which requires a workspace-local `typescript` package in node_modules — it fails with a clear "Could not find a valid TypeScript installation" error if `pnpm install`/`npm install` hasn't been run (or can't run, e.g. missing NODE_AUTH_TOKEN for private scoped packages). Get dependencies installed before expecting live TS diagnostics, not just before running tests.

complexity.codifies_existing_practice: This threshold was already the de facto convention -- every consuming repo's biome.json copied `"level": "error", "options": { "maxAllowedComplexity": 15 }` from platform-core's original config without eng-standards itself ever stating the number. Making it explicit here so it's a documented standard, not tribal knowledge passed repo-to-repo by copy-paste.

pr.description: Runs on every pull request — must pass before merge

steps.description: biome check — zero errors, zero warnings

merge.description: Runs on merge to main — full quality gate

pre_push.description: Blocks git push if typecheck, lint, or standards fail locally. Mirrors the PR gate exactly so CI is never the first to catch failures.
